rationale: mandel-2 is a small, floating-point-heavy numeric kernel (Mandelbrot iteration) dominated by a single very hot loop, so the priority is cheap data-flow obfuscation with minimal perturbation of the hot path: SUB and SPLIT get the highest weights because instruction substitution and basic-block splitting add strong static-analysis resistance at near-zero runtime and correctness cost on arithmetic-heavy code, while FLA and BCF are down-weighted heavily since flattening and bogus-control-flow on a tight iteration loop cause multiplicative slowdowns disproportionate to their security gain on a program this small; IBR is kept at a moderate weight to obscure the loop's branch structure without excessive indirect-branch overhead, and ICALL/IGV are kept low because mandel-2 has few calls and globals (n_functions unknown, no large function set), so those passes offer little diversity value here while still risking indirect-dispatch overhead; all CorrectnessRisk weights are held at or below 0.2 to preserve the exact FP iteration semantics the benchmark depends on.
